2026-12-03.title: Thursday after the Sunday of the Visitation · St Francis Xavier
2026-12-03.alt: St Francis Xavier, Jesuit priest and missionary (died 1552). He arrived in Goa in 1542 and preached along the coasts of South India, including Travancore, before going on to the Malay world and Japan (History). His body rests in Goa. The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo (Christmas), 1–24 December: prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
2026-12-03.verse: And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
theo: Paul, free in Christ, made himself a slave to all in order to win more of them: a Jew to the Jews, weak to the weak. “I have become all things to all people, that I might by all means save some.” This is the missionary's freedom: not changing the gospel, but changing himself, his comfort, his language and his habits, so that others can receive it.

The risen Lord rebukes the Eleven for their unbelief and then sends them anyway: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.” St Francis Xavier took those words to the letter. Sailing from Lisbon, he arrived in Goa in 1542, walked the fishing villages of South India, including the coast of Travancore, then went on to the Malay world and Japan. He died on an island off the coast of China, longing to enter it.

illus: A young Malankara Catholic engineer in Pune began inviting his colleagues from other states for Sunday lunch at his small flat. Over food they asked about his faith. Two years later one of them asked to be baptised.

homily: Dear friends, today we remember St Francis Xavier, the great missionary who preached on the coasts of South India. St Paul describes the heart of a missionary: though I am free with respect to all, I have made myself a slave to all, so that I might win more of them. I have become all things to all people, that I might by all means save some. I do it all for the sake of the gospel (1 Corinthians 9:19, 22–23).

Francis Xavier lived this. He learnt the prayers in the language of the fishermen, sat with the poor, nursed the sick, and walked from village to village. He became one with the people so that they might meet Christ.

In the Gospel the risen Jesus appears to the Eleven and says: go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation. And he promises signs: in my name they will cast out demons, speak in new tongues, lay hands on the sick and they will recover (Mark 16:15–18).
The mission is not finished. Many in our country and in the world have not truly heard the Gospel. Many baptised Christians have forgotten it. The Lord still says: go.

We are not all called to cross oceans, but we are all sent. A Malankara Catholic nurse in Germany, a student in Delhi, a worker in the Gulf, a farmer in Pathanamthitta: each can become all things to all people, out of love for Christ.
Let us pray today for missionaries, and for our own Church's mission in North India and abroad. And let us ask St Francis Xavier to give us his zeal and his joy. Amen.
